title: LinkedIn actually adds a ‘seems like AI slop’ button
slides: LinkedIn users can now flag AI-generated content.
But why would a professional network want this?
The button labels posts as 'seems like AI slop'.
Your feed will surface fewer low-effort AI posts.
Test it on a post you suspect is AI-generated.
thread_text:
1. Your feed’s new filter

LinkedIn added a button to flag posts as 'seems like AI slop' — and it will train the algorithm to show you fewer like that.

2. Why LinkedIn wants this

The network needs professional trust. AI-generated filler erodes engagement and makes the platform feel spammy.

3. The labeling mechanism

The flag doesn’t ban the post — it just adds a tag visible to you and reduces that type of content in your feed.

4. What happens to your data

Your clicks will train LinkedIn’s model to detect AI patterns across all users, not just your feed.

5. Test it this week

Find a post you suspect is AI-generated, click the flag, and see if your recommended content shifts in 24 hours.

instagram.caption:
LinkedIn just added a button that says 'seems like AI slop' to flag posts directly in your feed.

You click it, and the algorithm learns to show you fewer posts that look AI-generated. No bans, just a shift in your own recommendations.

If you create professional content, the platform is now signal-training against low-effort AI filler—your work gets surfaced over machine-glib fluff.

Is your feed already full of posts that read like a bad chatbot? Test the button on one this week.
